title: fleetfix.check/v1
description: One `fleetfix check` run. Consumers pin on the `schema` key, not on the binary version: adding a key is not a breaking change and consumers must ignore keys they do not know. Every key listed here is always present -- FleetFix never omits a key to mean empty -- so a consumer may read any documented path without an existence test. Removing a key, or changing the meaning of one, is what a v2 of this schema would be for.

schema.description: The document shape. Pin on this.

fleetfix_version.description: The binary that produced the report. Varies independently of `schema`.

generated_at.description: When the run finished: RFC 3339, UTC, three digits of subsecond, a literal Z. Truncated rather than rounded, so it never names a millisecond the run had not reached.

host.description: The machine the report is about: enough to identify it in an aggregation and to explain a platform-dependent result, and no more.

distro.description: The pretty name from os-release. Empty where the host has none -- empty, never a guess.

boot_id.description: Identifies this boot, so a consumer can tell an uptime reset from a rename. Empty where the kernel exposes none.

operator.description: Who ran the check. A cron job and a person debugging are different events, and the difference is worth seeing in an aggregation.

auth_principal.description: A vendor-neutral second-factor or SSO identity, populated out of band. FleetFix speaks no auth protocol and never synthesizes a value here, so this is empty unless something else set it.

source_ip.description: The client address from SSH_CONNECTION, empty on a local or non-SSH session.

privilege.description: What the process could do. Without it a skipped Tier 2 check is indistinguishable from a deselected one, and an unmonitored host looks like a healthy one.

can_tier2.description: Whether root-requiring checks could run: true for root, or for a working non-interactive sudo.

reason.description: Why can_tier2 is false, in the operator's terms. An expired cached credential reads very differently from a user not in sudoers. Empty when can_tier2 is true.

status.description: The worst status among the checks. A frozen enum: adding a seventh value is a breaking change, because every consumer switching on it has an else branch that would silently start catching the new one.

exit_code.description: The process exit code, monitoring-plugin convention. 0 ok, 1 warning, 2 critical, 3 unknown. `skipped` and `unavailable` exit 0: a host without docker is a supported host, not a paging event.

error.description: Why the run did not happen -- a config that would not parse, a selector that named nothing. Empty on every run that reached the checks, including one where individual checks errored; those explain themselves in checks[].error.

counts.description: How many checks landed in each status. Sums to the length of `checks`.

checks.description: One entry per check that was selected, ordered by id. Ordered rather than in completion order so two runs against an unchanged host produce the same bytes.

config_warnings.description: Every complaint the config layers produced, in the order they were found. In the document rather than on stderr because a cron job discards stderr, and a threshold ignored for a typo is exactly what makes a fleet quietly stop alerting.

status.description: ok: graded and fine. warn/crit: a threshold tripped. skipped: not attempted -- a missing privilege, an unsupplied parameter. unavailable: the host does not have what the check needs, which is a supported state and not a fault. error: the check itself broke, which is ranked above warn because an unnoticed broken check is how a fleet stays green while a disk fills.

id.description: The check's stable dotted identifier. Ids may be retired but are never repurposed, so an alert pinned to one can only ever stop matching -- it can never start matching something else.

summary.description: One line of plain text. Never markup: this is read by a terminal, a JSON consumer and a TUI, and only one of those can render markup.

trips.description: Every threshold this check crossed. Empty when nothing tripped.

metrics.description: The alerting contract. Names and labels are stable; this is what `--prom` emits and what an agent pushes.

data.description: Best-effort detail whose shape depends on `id`. Not a contract -- do not alert on it. Null where a check has nothing structured to add.

steps.description: What the check reported as it went, in order. The same events the TUI paints live. Empty for a check that produces its answer in one step.

error.description: Why this check failed, when its status is error. Empty otherwise.

rule.description: The threshold rule's id, which is also the key an operator overrides in thresholds.yml.

subject.description: What was measured, where a rule grades more than one thing: a mount point, an interface, a thermal zone. Empty for a host-wide rule.
